text:
Colorado's night in Ottawa was about much more than the point it took home. Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar both left with lower-body injuries, as Daily Faceoff reported, 57 seconds apart according to Corey Masisak of the Denver Post. No timeline has been given for either. Then the Avalanche came back from two down, took the lead, and lost 4-3 in overtime anyway.

Ottawa had the early edge on the scoreboard, if not on chances. Shane Pinto scored unassisted at 7:11 of the first and Tim Stützle finished at the side of the crease at 13:13. Colorado dragged it back with special teams. Artturi Lehkonen scored on the power play late in the second, and Parker Kelly, the undrafted former Senator, tied it shorthanded on a 3% chance early in the third. Gabriel Landeskog then put Colorado ahead on another power play at 10:03, a goal that lifted its win chance to 81%. The Avalanche went 2 for 5 with the man advantage; Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette notes their power play is at 26.8% since assistant Brett McLean took over.

Ottawa answered. Drake Batherson, who led everyone with six shots and 1.25 expected goals of his own, tied it with a backhand at 16:04, swinging the Senators from 11% to 52%. In overtime, a Kelly turnover put the puck on Pinto's stick in the slot, and he finished it at 2:08 for his second goal and third point. Linus Ullmark, back after a nine-game absence, made his biggest stop on Nazem Kadri earlier in overtime.

By our numbers Colorado had slightly the better of the night, with 2.93 expected goals to 2.55 and a 57% deserved-to-win share, but most of that came on the power play. At even strength the Senators had more, 1.83 to 1.33. Scott Wedgewood allowed 1.4 goals more than his 26 shots deserved.

For Ottawa, it is a comeback win and Ullmark back in net. For Colorado, the point is the least of it. Everything now waits on news about MacKinnon and Makar.
headline: Pinto wins it as Avalanche lose two stars
